profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at DocuSign
profile.summary:
I am extremely passionate about gaming (realtime systems as a whole, game development, and human computer interactions) and technology in general.

I am interested in machine learning, distributed systems, and challenging problems. In my free time, I program on various projects collaboratively and independently including various games and personal projects in an effort to grow as an engineer and individual.  

I am not interested in front-end web development as my primary work.

Specialties: C#, C++11, C,SQL,Python, Systems Architecture, Unity, Game Development (Engine and some design), Networking, Big Data, Monitoring, NoSQL, NodeJS/React and Code Generation

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Working on Microsoft Advertising’s delivery engine  on a petabyte scale streaming infrastructure written primarily using C# 4.5, C/C++11, and SQL

Although I have worked on most projects within the scope of my team, I primary lead, design, develop, test, and maintain a fully asynchronous monitoring and alerting framework used by multiple services and multiple teams to facilitate cross-team, cross-datacenter  data integrity, and quality validations for our delivery engine and serving stack which helps detect costly live-site errors. C++, C#, SQL, Azure, REST

-Work with partner teams to on-board onto common data platform and monitoring infrastructures
-Mentor and train new employees
-Participate on on-call live site response and mitigation
-Deploy live-site code
-Debug, mitigate, resolve, and implement automated repair mechanisms for live site data integrity and quality issues

projects.title: Monitoring and Alerting
projects.description:
Designed and Developed and tested a Monitoring and Alerting system for SQL and HTTP services:
- Features a generic design that uses a plugin model to run appropriate tasks and gather data or heal the system
- Alerts using a generic rules engine that takes reported data points and converts them into a useful efficient alert-time evaluation (<1 sec)
- Added AlwaysOn availability groups reducing calls to the team due to transient network and physical issues. This increased the database up-time by 30% and has been running without issues since Spring 2014
- Added the ability to gather datasource data in parallel and asynchronously reducing the time of pulling data from ~5 min to ~45 sec and can pull approximately 1-2 GB/min consistently.
- Reduced alert noise by fixing invalid alerts at system creation.
It combines all requirements of 
- Exposed, gathered and created reports for data trends and for our various data streams allowing us to know exactly how many entities are active and have been updated during a given time-frame. This has proven extremely beneficial in tracking down issues instantly in the data pipeline that previously were day's worth of manual effort and added automated alerting when suspicious trends occur in a given set of data.
